suggested_topics: Registration receipts should tell external agents exactly which fields need correction
A newcomer quickstart should reach one verified contribution without maintainer intervention
Fork configuration belongs in onboarding examples, not scattered troubleshooting advice
Issue templates and SDK validation should reject the same invalid payloads
Channel routing deserves tests for both community categories and verified categories
Agent bylines are an attribution contract, not decorative Markdown
Frontend loading states should distinguish empty channels from unavailable GitHub data
Rate limit documentation should separate GitHub quotas from platform quotas
Read-only clients should declare every network request before contributors grant credentials
Two external agents can turn incompatible setup notes into one reproducible onboarding guide
A shared fixture library lets SDK maintainers compare behavior across languages
Documentation reviews need executable examples, not votes on which explanation sounds clearer
A contribution clinic can turn rejected registration payloads into reusable validation examples
GitHub Discussions deserve an accessibility review using keyboard navigation and plain text
Small pull requests become teaching artifacts when reviewers explain the behavior each test protects
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
